# Results — Study 631 (Restatement Shock, Item 4.02)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **an 8-K
saying "do not rely on our financials" keeps hurting for months; the market underreacts to
accounting bombs** — measured as a market-adjusted event study on Item 4.02 8-Ks pulled from
EDGAR full-text search. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete month; every drift window
ends on or before it). Close-panel fingerprint `9b979967dc4c`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Events | **1,498** Item-4.02 8-Ks (structured `items` contains `4.02`), EDGAR FTS, 2004-09-01 → 2026-06-17, sampled per quarter with deterministic quarter-stratified thinning to the 1,500 cap |
| Ticker mapping | **520** events (35%) map to a ticker (FTS display name, else SEC current `company_tickers.json`) |
| Usable events | **359** (ticker on the yfinance tape + 60d pre-history + complete 63d post window); close panel 5,658 days × 367 names, 2004-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Benchmark | SPY (total-return, yfinance); abnormal return = stock log return − SPY log return |
| Windows | announcement **[0,+1]**; drift **[+2,+64]** = 63 trading days ≈ 3 months, entry at the **close of day +1** (the single documented execution lag) |
| Costs | short overlay: one-way bps × 2 legs on the stock + 1 bp × 2 on SPY + **borrow** × 63/252 (shorts pay borrow) |

> **Deads-missing bias (named on the Signal axis).** The CIK→ticker map is *current* and
> yfinance has no delisted history: **1,139 of 1,498** events drop out (no ticker / no tape).
> Post-confession **bankruptcies** are among the dropped — the worst drift outcomes — so every
> negative number below is an **understatement** of the true damage. The bias is strongest for
> *old* events (a 2005 filer still mapped today is a 20-year survivor), which is visible in the
> era split.

## The bomb — announcement window [0,+1]

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean AR[0,+1] | **−2.32%** vs SPY (median −0.66%) |
| per-event *t* | −3.17 |
| winsorized (1%/99%) *t* | **−4.55** |
| month-clustered NW-HAC *t* | **−2.27** |

The confession costs ~2.3% versus the market in two days and clears the bar on every
statistic — **certified**. (And trimmed of its worst cases by the deads-missing bias.)

## The drift — [+2,+64], the actual claim

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean CAR[+2,+64] | **−15.84%** (median −5.86%; 62.4% of events negative) |
| per-event *t* | −4.01 (overlap-inflated — refused as headline) |
| winsorized *t* | −5.06 |
| **month-clustered NW-HAC *t*** | **−4.41** (162 event-months) |

Penny-floor robustness (entry price at day +1): ≥ $1 → n=289, CAR **−13.41%**, HAC *t* =
−4.20; ≥ $5 → n=228, CAR **−12.97%**, HAC *t* = −3.54. Not a sub-penny artifact.

Horizon curve (entry close +1): +5d −0.75% (HAC −1.17) · +21d −6.27% (HAC −2.70) · +42d
−8.54% (HAC −2.86) · **+63d −15.84% (HAC −4.41)** · +126d −23.90% (HAC −4.47).

So the raw post-confession bleed is large and statistically loud. **But:**

## The adversarial control — chronic-decay placebo (the verdict-maker)

Firms that file 4.02s are disproportionately chronically-bleeding microcaps. For each usable
event we measure the **same stock's** market-adjusted CAR over a same-length (63d) window
entered **252 trading days before** the event entry — a no-event window. Only the **paired
difference** can certify that the *confession* causes the drift.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| paired events | 324 |
| event-window CAR | −17.49% (*t* = −4.07) |
| **placebo-window CAR (no event, same stocks)** | **−13.13%** (*t* = −4.27) |
| **event-specific drift (paired difference)** | **−4.36%** · paired *t* = **−0.85** · winsorized *t* = −0.93 · HAC *t* = −0.63 |

The stocks that confess were **already melting at ~the same rate in a random pre-event
window**. The event-specific increment (−4.4%) has the right sign but is nowhere near *t* ≥ 2.
**The underreaction claim is not certified — the "drift" is mostly composition, not causation.**

## Era split

| era | n | announcement (HAC *t*) | drift (per-event *t*, HAC *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2004-2012 | 92 | −0.40% (−0.48) | −2.81% (−0.64, −0.28) |
| 2013-2026 | 267 | −2.98% (−2.28) | −20.33% (−4.02, −5.13) |

The early era is flat — exactly where the survivor-mapping bias is strongest (only 20-year
survivors remain) — and the modern era carries everything (SPAC-era microcaps). Consistent
with both the named bias and the chronic-decay reading; not with a stable, exploitable
underreaction.

## Third axis — is the drift concentrated in small caps (limits-to-arbitrage)?

Median split on pre-event median dollar volume ([−65,−6]; split at **$0.18M/day** — this is a
microcap panel throughout).

| half | n | drift CAR | *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SMALL (illiquid) | 180 | **−21.80%** | −3.32 | −3.60 |
| LARGE (liquid) | 179 | −9.85% | −2.27 | −1.56 |

Welch *t* of the difference = **−1.52**. Direction exactly as Shleifer-Vishny predicts, but the
halves are not separable at *t* ≥ 2 — and the placebo shows the drift isn't event-specific in
the first place. **MIXED.**

## Tradability — short the confession (modeled)

Short at close +1, cover at +64, SPY-hedged; shorts pay borrow.

| terms (one-way, borrow) | gross/event | drag | net/event | net *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps, 3%/yr | +15.84% | 0.97% | +14.87% | +3.77 | +4.09 |
| 20 bps, 10%/yr | +15.84% | 2.92% | +12.92% | +3.27 | +3.45 |
| 50 bps, 25%/yr | +15.84% | 7.27% | +8.57% | +2.17 | +2.03 |

The *modeled* net survives — but the edge is **not the event** (event-specific part: −4.4%,
*t* = −0.85); it is generic short-melting-microcap exposure. And the vehicle is unshortable in
practice: median pre-event dollar volume **$0.18M/day**, sub-$1 names, scandal borrow (locates
scarce or unavailable, buy-in risk, fees far beyond the modeled grid), capacity ≈ nil.
**MIRAGE** — what survives on paper is not the claimed edge and not accessible at size.

## Synthetic machinery control (never cited as market evidence)

| planted world | raw drift (HAC *t*) | event-specific (paired *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (drift 0, chronic 0) | +0.83% (+1.48) | +0.92% (+0.71) |
| TRUE underreaction (−8% drift) | −7.17% (**−8.80**) | −7.08% (**−5.42**) |
| chronic bleed only (−40%/yr, no event effect) | −9.17% (**−11.37**) | +0.92% (+0.71) |

The raw drift detector false-fires on a melting-ice-cube world; the paired placebo correctly
refuses it and correctly certifies a true underreaction. The real tape looks like row 3, not
row 2 — and the machinery can tell them apart.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED** (split spelled out): **Real on the bomb** — AR[0,+1] = −2.32%, HAC
  *t* = −2.27, winsorized *t* = −4.55. **Not certified on the underreaction drift** — the raw
  −15.84% (HAC *t* = −4.41) collapses to **−4.36% at paired *t* = −0.85** against the
  same-stock chronic-decay placebo: the confessing stocks were dying anyway. Deads-missing
  bias **named**: the true post-event damage is worse than this survivor-tilted tape can show,
  but a stamp needs the tape we have.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The modeled short survives costs, but the surviving edge is
  chronic microcap decay (not the event), on unshortable sub-$1M/day scandal names.
- **Small-cap story? — MIXED.** −21.80% (small) vs −9.85% (large), the limits-to-arbitrage
  direction, Welch *t* = −1.52 — not separable, and not event-specific anyway.
